newsitem.title: UK: Less confidence in Italy, Denmark in EMU - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Less confidence in Italy, Denmark in EMU - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of Italy and Denmark taking part in European Monetary Union retreated over the past week while EMU expectations in Sweden edged higher, JP Morgan's EMU calculator showed.
The U.S. investment house's method of calculating market expectations of EMU taking place monitors bond yield spreads in the swaps market between participating European countries.

The latest calculation shows the probability of Italy participating in EMU fell 6.0 percentage points to 56 percent in the five trading days to Friday but was still up a net 4.0 points over the past 20 days.
Denmark's EMU probability retreated 7.0 points to 45 percent last week, but was also up a net 1.0 over 20 days.
Sweden rose 3.0 points to 64 percent over the past five days, to bring its increase over 20 days to a net 2.0 points.
Elsewhere, probabilities in the U.K. and Spain crept up 1.0 point each last week.
According to these calculations, the market still believes in a 100-percent chance of France and Belgium being in EMU and that was unchanged from last week.

The calculator works by assigning a market probability level to each country. This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
